newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to launch OTC stock market.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to launch OTC stock market.

text.p: Malaysia on Tuesday unveiled plans for an over-the-counter (OTC) stock market that will enable high-technology firms with no track record to raise capital.

Modelled on electronic markets such as NASDAQ in the United States, the Malaysian Exchange of Securities Dealing and Automated Quotation (MESDAQ) was expected to be launched before the end of the year, Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
"It is imperative that all parties ensure the market is up and running before the end of the year," Anwar said in a speech on Tuesday at an OTC conference.
Securities Commission chairman Munir Majid said the new market was expected to play a role similar to that of NASDAQ in the U.S. information technology sector.
"It has been recognised that the dynamics of the NASDAQ market is a key component in the development of the software industry," he said while announcing details on MESDAQ.

"The proposed new market will be independent of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE), and will cater for technology based companies, and companies with strong growth potential, but which do not have a profit track record," he said.
They included those involved in advanced electronics, biotechnology, information technology, aerospace technology and telecommunications, he said.
MESDAQ would operate in a full disclosure-based regulatory environment, Munir said.
He said Malaysian and foreign-owned companies, businesses within Malaysia and outside could be listed on MESDAQ. This included 100 percent foreign-owned companies.
At least 70 percent of the funds raised via MESDAQ must be invested in Malaysia, he said.
Companies seeking listing on MESDAQ must have a minimum paid-up capital of two million ringgit ($803,000) with no ceiling, Munir said.
He said the price of the securities to be offered would be determined and agreed upon between the applicant and underwriters.
Malaysia also hopes MESDAQ will help promote its ambitious plan to be a multimedia centre.
"We want Malaysia to be able to demonstrate that the MSC initiative is being followed through," Anwar said.

The MSC, or Multimedia Super Corridor, conceived by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, is a proposed 15 by 40 km (nine by 25 mile) corridor stretching south from Kuala Lumpur to a new airport and administrative capital.
Malaysia has been courting U.S. high-technology firms and hopes to attract a variety of vendors to the MSC.
Analysts generally welcomed the introduction of the new market though some said the initial response may be slow.

"It's obviously a very forward looking move. But in the context of technology companies in Malaysia, it could be a little premature. Technology companies have to gestate for a while before they go public," said Bernard Tan, an electronics analyst at Merrill Lynch in Singapore.

Dominic Armstrong, head of research at Pesaka Jardine Fleming, said: "It's perfect for the small companies in the MSC. If Malaysia is going to be a capital of the information technology industry in Asia, this is highly appropriate."
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
($1=2.49 ringgit)
